question.problem:
The weights of some chocolate cookies are normally distributed with a mean of $10\,\text{g}$ and a variance of $1\,{\text{g}}^{2}.$
On the other hand, the weights of some oatcakes are normally distributed with a mean of $15\,\text{g}$ and a variance of $2\,{\text{g}}^{2},$ while the weights of some macaroons are normally distributed with a mean of $14\,\text{g}$ and a variance of $1.5\,{\text{g}}^{2}.$ 

If one chocolate cookie, one oatcake, and one macaroon are randomly selected, what is the probability that the sum of $6$ times the weight of the cookie and $5$ times the weight of the oatcake is less than $10$ times the weight of the macaroon? You may assume that the weights are independent. 

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.1\,$ | $\,0.5398\,$ | $\,0.5438\,$ | $\,0.5478\,$ | $\,0.5517\,$ | $\,0.5557\,$ |
| $\,0.2\,$ | $\,0.5793\,$ | $\,0.5832\,$ | $\,0.5871\,$ | $\,0.5910\,$ | $\,0.5948\,$ |
| $\,0.3\,$ | $\,0.6179\,$ | $\,0.6217\,$ | $\,0.6255\,$ | $\,0.6293\,$ | $\,0.6331\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let ${X}_{1}$, ${X}_{2},$ and ${X}_{3}$ denote the weight of the chocolate cookie, the oatcake, and the macaroon, respectively. Then, we have

$$
{X}_{1}∼N(10,1),\,{X}_{2}∼N(15,2),\,{X}_{3}∼N(14,1.5).
$$

Let the random variable $Y$ denote the difference between the sum of $6$ times the weight of the cookie and $5$ times the weight of the oatcake, and $10$ times the weight of the macaroon. Then, we have $Y=6{X}_{1}+5{X}_{2}-10{X}_{3},$ and we want to find 

$$
P(Y<0).
$$

The random variable $Y$ is normally distributed, where

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & =(6\cdot 10+4\cdot 15-10\cdot 14) \\  & =-5 \\ \text{Var}[Y] & ={6}^{2}\cdot 1+{5}^{2}\cdot 2+{10}^{2}\cdot 1.5 \\  & =36+50+150 \\  & =236.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
Y∼N(-5,236).
$$

In order to find $P(Y<0),$ we convert $Y$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y<0) & =P(Z<\frac{0-(-5)}{\sqrt{236}}) \\  & ≈P(Z<0.33) \\  & =Φ(0.33)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(0.33)≈0.6293.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y<0) & ≈Φ(0.33) \\  & ≈0.6293.\end{aligned}
$$
